messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: DETECTED p95/p99 LATENCY SURGE for model redwood-small-int8-v2 on /v1/generate. window=1m, p95=480ms (baseline ~120ms), p99=2100ms (baseline ~480ms). Streaming session stalls and partial chunk timeouts flagged. Auto-calibration rollout 'quant-int8-v2' deployed ~03:10Z. Paging oncall.

sam-oc: on it. joining bridge now. can someone paste the last deploy id and the calib change?

morgan-ml: that rollout is the one I pushed this morning, id qc-20260315-07. It toggles per-layer int8 kernels and enables an alternate dequant path for KV cache. saw small perf win in canary but not this extreme. investigating logs.

jordan-sre: grabbing traces. looks like a spike in dequant kernel time on GPU nodes rwd-gpu-14/15. stack shows repeated memcpy + dequant op at request tail. streaming sessions show long gaps (500ms+ between chunks). attaching a quick snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T03:12:01Z] req=0x7f9a dequant_ms=720 kernel_copy_ms=110 total_tail_ms=840
[2026-03-15T03:12:01Z] req=0x8a3 dequant_ms=640 kernel_copy_ms=98 total_tail_ms=760
```

lee-eng: that matches what I saw in perf dashboard — a small subset of hosts show dequant timings 10x higher. suspecting a mixed-precision path hit (int8->fp32) that falls back to a slower kernel when cache layout doesn't match.

morgan-ml: good call. also seeing KV prefix cache miss rates spike and a lot of short-lived sessions forcing cache rebuilds. if the new dequant path expects packed KV layout, a mismatch could trigger expensive path.

sam-oc: action list: 1) immediate traffic routing fallback to fp16 variant 2) pause/rollback calibration rollout 3) isolate affected hosts 4) gather sample request ids for repro + notify customers. I'll do 1 and 2 now. jordan please open bridge and tag ops-bot for automated routing command.

jordan-sre: bridge created -> https://meet/bridge/1823456789. ops-bot, run routing fallback to prefer redwood-small-fp16 for production /v1/generate (weight override).

ops-bot: running routing update -> set model_routing.override(redwood-small-int8-v2 => redwood-small-fp16) weight=85% scope=global.

ops-bot: routing update applied at 2026-03-15T03:13:20Z.

jordan-sre: watching metrics. initial effect within 30s: p99 dropped from 2.1s -> 640ms, p95 -> 160ms. Streaming stall reports decreasing but still a few hosts with residual high tail.

morgan-ml: starting rollback of calib qc-20260315-07 to qc-20260314-09 (previous stable). command: `/ci rollback-calib --profile qc-20260314-09 --target redwood-small-int8-v2`

lee-eng: executing rollback now on control plane. will patch config on private clusters then public. ETA ~90s.

ops-bot: calib rollback job started (job=rb-1823456789). logs: job queued -> deploying rollback -> applying on 12 clusters.

ops-bot: calib rollback completed at 2026-03-15T03:14:55Z. verification running.

jordan-sre: post-rollback metrics: p99=360ms, p95=140ms across 90% of hosts. remaining 10% are catch-up nodes with higher dequant latency but no new customer errors reported.

emily-pm: customer impact: CSMs notified for customers with strict streaming SLOs (acme-corp, mindful-chat). ACME reported 2 brief degraded calls; no data loss. timeline for notification sent.

sam-oc: good. can we confirm whether this was a rollout gating failure (canary size too small) or an unexpected interaction with older KV cache versions on some hosts? morgan, what's the root suspicion?

morgan-ml: preliminary: two-fold issue — (A) rollout had insufficient vertical canary (only CPU/pred nodes) and missed GPU-specific dequant path; (B) nodes running older KV cache serialization (v1.2) hit an untested branch in the new dequant kernel causing memcpy fallback.

lee-eng: we'll schedule a quick forced rebuild of KV cache format v1.2 nodes and add a config check in the rollout pipeline to block if cache_version != expected. also add a per-host metric for dequant_ms to alert earlier.

jordan-sre: follow-ups for postmortem: - timeline and signal detection - why canary didn't catch GPU regression - add gating to calib rollout pipeline - automated revert on p99>800ms for 3m - customer comms template

sam-oc: for immediate mitigation checklist: - keep routing override for 2 hours while we finish sweep - cordon affected hosts and repro in staging - add a streaming-specific synthetic that validates chunk cadence (every 200ms)

emily-pm: CSMs asked for ETA on permanent fix and whether we'll revise SLAs for next maintenance window. I'll coordinate and put a short note in updates channel after postmortem draft.

morgan-ml: repro notes saved under /s3/triage/1823456789/samples (request ids 0x7f9a, 0x8a3, 0x8b1). will run a targeted microbench against dequant kernel on repro hosts.

lee-eng: one more immediate safety: disable auto-calibration rollouts across prod until we add cache-version gating. created internal ticket INF-3482.

ops-bot: routing override will auto-unstage at 2026-03-15T05:13:20Z unless extended.

sam-oc: bridge standing by. final status: primary mitigations applied (routing fallback + calib rollback). p95/p99 back within acceptable range for majority of traffic. keeping oncall until 03:45Z to watch for regressions. thanks all for quick responses. :thumbsup:

jordan-sre: note to self — include kernel-level histograms in next deck so we can spot multimodal latencies earlier.

emily-pm: I'll draft customer-facing blurb and share in 15m. postmortem owners: jordan (SRE), morgan (ML), lee (eng).

sam-oc: standing down bridge at 03:45Z unless new alerts. will follow up in #postmortems with write-up.

ops-bot: bridge closed at 2026-03-15T03:45:01Z. incident marked: mitigated -> monitoring.
